items.text: I can explain the 3-tier web application architecture and the role of each tier
I know the difference between Apache/Nginx (frontend web servers) and Node.js/Flask (backend app servers)
I can define the three types of Linux software: system, application, and utility
I understand what a software package contains (program files, dependencies, config files, metadata)
I can explain what a repository is and who maintains them (Amazon, Canonical, third-party)
I know the difference between YUM (Amazon Linux/Red Hat) and APT (Ubuntu/Debian)
I can explain the difference between yum update (refresh metadata) and yum upgrade (install newer versions)
I can define OS patching and explain why it is critical for security
I can install a software package using sudo yum install <package> -y
I can check if software is installed using <software> --version or yum info <package>
I can refresh repository metadata with sudo yum update -y
I can check for available updates with sudo yum check-update <package>
I can locate repository configuration files in /etc/yum.repos.d/
I can install multiple packages in a single YUM command
I can install, start, and verify an Apache web server on Amazon Linux
I can answer: What package manager does Amazon Linux use? (YUM)
I can answer: What is the difference between yum update and yum upgrade?
I can answer: What does a Linux software repository contain?
I can answer: Which tier does Apache/Nginx belong to in 3-tier architecture? (Frontend/Tier 1)
I can answer: Where are repository config files stored on Amazon Linux? (/etc/yum.repos.d/)
I can answer: What does OS patching mean and why is it necessary?
I can answer: What AWS service automates patching across EC2 instances? (AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager)
